findings: ETT.tex:1940–1941: 'The map M → A∩B is a Cauchy embedding, so φ(Σ) is a Cauchy surface of A∩B' is true on ETT's spacetimes (Hausdorff, second countable, any causality: IsCauchyEmbedding.isCauchySurfaceOn_inf_of_secondCountable), but the paper gives no argument, and the argument needs three things the paper never states: (i) every inextensible causal curve c of A∩B, after trimming its constant end pieces, is a reparametrised sub-arc of an inextensible curve of A and of one of B (the sub-arc form of the Zorn curves theorem; second countability); (ii) trimming keeps c inextensible in A∩B; (iii) the end-point argument. If the curve of A meets φ(Σ) after c and the one of B before it, a segment of each concatenates to a causal curve of N meeting φ(Σ) twice unless c meets it (N causal). If both meet it after c, then either c has a last value, at which the curve of A meets φ(Σ) or which it leaves inside A∩B for a new value (contradicting inextensibility), or c has a limit at its end; that limit lies in A∖B for the curve of A and in B∖A for the curve of B, and Hausdorffness makes the two limits equal. Suggested wording: 'every inextensible causal curve of A∩B lies, reparametrised, on inextensible causal curves of A and of B, which meet φ(Σ); if none meets it on the curve, both leave A∩B through its end point, which would lie in (A∖B)∩(B∖A)'.

ETT.tex:1940: the 'so' runs the wrong way. By def:cauchy_embedding_cauchy_extension (ETT.tex:1858–1861), that M → A∩B is a Cauchy embedding includes that some Cauchy surface of M is carried onto a Cauchy surface of A∩B, and that A∩B is globally hyperbolic. So the Cauchy-surface statement is what has to be proved, not a consequence (lem:Cauchy_plongement_toutes then gives it for every Σ). The global hyperbolicity of A∩B is not argued either: here it comes from the causal convexity of A∩B in N, with N causally arc-connected (isCauchyInclusion_inf_of_secondCountable).
questions: OQ-94 (open, not decided here): may the abstract form anchor the row? Reading taken: abstract setting, nothing marked, and 'what_it_would_anchor' states what each form would anchor if it may.

'The map M → A∩B is a Cauchy embedding' read as IsCauchyInclusion D hφ.rangeOpens (A ⊓ B), the inclusion of φ(M) ≅ M (φ is an open embedding) into A∩B. The global hyperbolicity it includes is proved only with N causally arc-connected (a fact of singular flat spacetimes, SingularFlatAxioms.causallyArcConnected, in the geometric reading). Without hDac, whether A∩B is globally hyperbolic in the abstract setting is not decided here.

sub_arc_lemma.name: Causal.Causality.exists_subArc_of_t1_secondCountable
sub_arc_lemma.statement: [T1Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M], C.CausalCurveIn W I c → ∃ I₀ ⊆ I, ∃ ρ : ℝ → ℝ, I₀.Nonempty ∧ I₀.OrdConnected ∧ TailFree I₀ c ∧ MapsTo ρ I I₀ ∧ MonotoneOn ρ I ∧ (∀ t ∈ I₀, ρ t = t) ∧ (∀ t ∈ I, c (ρ t) = c t) ∧ ∃ J γ ψ, C.Inextensible W J γ ∧ TailFree J γ ∧ StrictMonoOn ψ I₀ ∧ ContinuousOn ψ I₀ ∧ MapsTo ψ I₀ J ∧ (ψ '' I₀).OrdConnected ∧ ∀ t ∈ I₀, γ (ψ t) = c t
sub_arc_lemma.reading: the trimmed curve is γ ∘ ψ on the sub-interval I₀ and constant off it (c = c ∘ ρ, ρ a monotone retraction onto I₀, continuous by continuousOn_of_retraction; c '' I₀ = c '' I by image_eq_of_retraction)
sub_arc_lemma.companions: Causal.Causality.exists_subArc_of_tailFree (a tail-free curve is γ ∘ ψ on all of I); Causal.Causality.Inextensible.exists_subArc_of_le (an inextensible curve of W ≤ U, trimmed, is still inextensible in W, tail-free, same image, and a sub-arc of an inextensible curve of U); Causal.Causality.Inextensible.of_retraction (trimming keeps inextensibility, no separation axiom)

kb_proposals: The sub-arc form of the curves theorem: Causal.Causality.exists_subArc_of_t1_secondCountable (T1, second countable): a causal curve, trimmed to I₀ and constant off it (c = c ∘ ρ), is γ ∘ ψ on I₀ for an inextensible, tail-free γ and ψ strictly increasing, continuous, with ordconnected image. Also _of_tailFree, and Inextensible.exists_subArc_of_le for an inextensible curve of W ≤ U. This answers kb/0212's 'image containment only' (CausalScaffold.CExtConnexeCauchy.SubArc).

Constant end pieces do not affect inextensibility: Causal.Causality.Inextensible.of_retraction (inextensible over I ⇒ inextensible over the trimmed I₀ of exists_tailFree_retraction; no separation axiom), through Extensible.of_top_tail / of_bottom_tail, which pause the old extension with pauseTop and CausalCurveIn.comp_monotoneOn (a causal curve read through a continuous non-decreasing reparametrisation).

Causal.Causality.causalCurveIn_comp_monotoneOn (Causal/Remarks/SingularRowsCauchyExt.lean:191) is model-free but stranded in a model module (kb/0061). Its ETT-layer twin, under a distinct name, is Causal.Causality.CausalCurveIn.comp_monotoneOn (CExtConnexeCauchy.SubArc). Merge at the next hoist.

A Cauchy surface of M (causal, T2, second countable) that is Cauchy in the opens A and B is Cauchy in A ∩ B: Causal.Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_inf_of_secondCountable. The end-point step, usable elsewhere: Inextensible.mem_image_or_tendsto_of_above / _below (a sub-arc relation c = γ ∘ ψ, plus a parameter s of γ after ψ(I), gives γ(s) ∈ c(I) or a limit of c at its end outside W).

Time-reversing a whole sub-arc configuration (curve c ↦ c(-·), interval I ↦ -I, map ψ ↦ -ψ(-·), parameter s ↦ -s): Inextensible.dual_reverse, CausalCurveIn.reverse, TailFree.neg, ordConnected_image_neg. Inextensible.mem_image_or_tendsto_of_below is the pattern: one application of the future form to C.dual, then simpa [neg_neg].
inextensible_nested ⇒ curve_nested on T1, second countable spaces: Causal.Causality.InextensibleNestedOn.curveNestedOn_of_t1_secondCountable (the ladder's [[open]] pair-sort entry).
